<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command executes only the top-level code in the PKGBUILD file. Examining the file, there are no dangerous top-level commands such as `exec`, `bash`, `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or any other code that would download or execute untrusted payloads. The PKGBUILD contains standard AUR metadata (pkgname, pkgver, source, etc.) and build functions (prepare, build, check, package) that are not executed by this command. The only VCS source is defined via `source=("$_pkgname::git+$url.git")` which is standard for AUR packages and does not pose a security risk at this stage. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is a SKIPped checksum, which is explicitly allowed per the security guidelines (missing or SKIPped checksums are never grounds to fail this gate). Since no malicious or potentially dangerous code is present in the top-level scope, `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe to run.
</details>
